title: Day 4 Knowledge Check: Structured JSON & Tool Execution

questions.question: Why validate SLM tool arguments with Pydantic before calling downstream APIs or webhooks?

options.A: To catch malformed JSON, missing keys, or invalid types deterministically before triggering side effects.
options.B: To speed up cosine similarity math in Qdrant.

questions.explanation: Pydantic acts as a deterministic type firewall between probabilistic LLM text and real operational APIs.
questions.implication: Unvalidated LLM strings passed directly to Kubernetes or billing APIs can trigger destructive automation on hallucinated parameters.

questions.question: What is a major operational drawback of letting an agent chain many sequential tool/API calls?

options.A: Latency multiplies per round-trip, raw JSON responses bloat context tokens, and flaky APIs can cause retry loops.
options.C: Tool calls cannot be traced in OpenTelemetry.

questions.explanation: Every tool call adds round-trip latency and tokens—requiring max_steps bounds and span monitoring.
questions.implication: Production agents need strict step budgets, tool output truncation, and OpenTelemetry span timers per tool call.

questions.question: How does ModelRouter handle response_schema when running locally vs. on Vertex AI?

options.A: It injects a JSON key template into the system prompt locally, and uses native response_schema on Vertex AI.

questions.explanation: This preserves a single unified interface across local SLMs and managed cloud APIs.
questions.implication: Application code stays completely decoupled from provider-specific structured-output SDK quirks.
